analysis.title: Six Flags (FUN): Takeaways from meeting with management
key_insights: Management is evaluating sales of parks that no longer fit the broader strategy, including larger parks, and of underlying land. Inbound and outbound discussions are underway with park and land buyers.
The bar for selling a core or top-tier park is much higher. Any sale would need a multiple high enough to more than offset the EBITDA sold and meaningfully improve leverage.
Management sees portfolio rationalization as a key lever to improve liquidity and move toward its ~4x leverage target.
FUN is in active discussions with its Six Flags Over Georgia (SFOG) partners about an upcoming ~$370mn payment. A formal update is expected, likely before year-end.

Management says it has enough liquidity to fund the Georgia obligation in full if needed, through revolver availability and additional secured debt capacity. Timing flexibility on growth capex is a further lever, though management does not expect to need it.
After Georgia, attention shifts to Six Flags Over Texas, where the obligation is ~$228mn and partner discussions are at a much earlier stage.
Maintenance capex is only ~20%-30% of total capex, giving FUN flexibility in how it deploys the rest of the budget.
Growth projects are evaluated park by park on expected returns, and lower-return projects are re-sequenced rather than automatically going ahead.
Management still sees value in larger rides for visitation lift but is directing more growth capital to events, attractions, comfort and amenities, where the benefit is more sustained.

Management sees attendance growth as critical to longer-term earnings. Levers are marketing and social media, events and entertainment, and guest experience. Cross-park visitation has risen significantly.
Per cap growth is targeted through merchandising and food, and better in-park entertainment to encourage repeat visits.
Costs are one of the more visible pieces of the 2027 algorithm. Savings are expected first to offset inflation and reinvestment, with any remainder going to the bottom line.

Savings are described as an ongoing process across procurement, contract renegotiation, support center optimization and labor. FUN is making its seasonal and temporary labor more flexible with attendance and looking at eliminating or automating work.
Management added a new Chief Procurement Officer and rebuilt the FP&A function.
GS rates FUN Neutral with a 12-month price target of $9, based on 7.5X 2027E EV/EBITDA. The target is 24.2% below the $11.88 close on 19 Nov 2026.

market_movers.rationale: The 12-month PT of $9 is based on 7.5X 2027E EV/EBITDA, 24.2% below the $11.88 close. The meeting tone was constructive, with no change to rating or target.

earnings_insights: GS estimates for FUN: 2026E revenue $2,823.7mn and EBITDA $755.3mn. 2027E revenue $2,949.2mn and EBITDA $804.3mn. 2028E revenue $3,060.8mn and EBITDA $847.4mn.
GS EPS estimates (GS Research forecast): 2026E $(8.46), 2027E $(0.78), 2028E $(0.69). Quarterly estimates: 12/26E $(0.65), 3/27E $(2.27), 6/27E $0.02. Reported 9/26 EPS $(3.59).
GS EV/EBITDA estimates: 7.8X 2026E, 7.7X 2027E, 7.3X 2028E. Net debt/EBITDA is 6.2X in 2026E and 2027E and 5.8X in 2028E.
Management sees a compelling opportunity in 2027 and beyond to grow attendance and per caps and to drive cost savings to offset inflation, while being more selective on growth capex.
risk_factors: Greater than expected ability to capture market share (upside risk to estimates or valuation view).
More limited impact on margins from reinvestment (upside risk).
Lower than expected per cap growth (downside risk).
Liquidity and leverage: the ~$370mn SFOG payment and ~$228mn Six Flags Over Texas obligation against a ~4x leverage target, with GS forecasting net debt/EBITDA of 6.2X in 2026E and 2027E.
